- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10% in the first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — apply a dampening factor (e.g., 0.85) to subsequent days post-peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in the 10–15 day window; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) in all examples — no behavioral signal to adjust for; if sentiment later becomes positive or negative, adjust forecast slope accordingly (e.g., +2% for positive sentiment, -1% for negative).
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often lag true trend by 2–4 days; if true outcome shows a clear directional shift (e.g., upward) within first 5 days, model should adjust forecast to match that trend earlier.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3–5 days are volatile, don’t extrapolate too far ahead; use 7-day moving average as a smoothing anchor.
